title: Mathematics — Final Assessment
subject: Mathematics
description: Grade 2 end-of-year maths final: number, operations, measurement, data, fractions, and multiplication.

sections.name: Addition & Subtraction
sections.instruction: Work out each sum carefully. Line up your hundreds, tens, and ones!

questions.hint: Start with the ones: 5 + 8 = 13. Carry the 1 ten over to the tens column!
No carrying needed here. Add the ones, then the tens, then the hundreds.
In the ones, 2 is smaller than 7, so borrow 1 ten to make 12 − 7.
No borrowing needed. Take away the ones, then the tens, then the hundreds.

questions.prompt: Word problem: Maya picked 156 mangoes and Sam picked 128 mangoes. How many mangoes did they pick altogether?
questions.hint: Altogether means add! 156 + 128. Remember to carry when the ones make more than 9.

sections.name: Place Value & Number Names
sections.instruction: Think about hundreds, tens, and ones.

questions.hint: The 3 is worth 300, the 4 is worth 40, and the 2 is worth 2.

questions.prompt: Write this number in figures: two hundred and sixteen.
questions.hint: Two hundred is 200. Then add sixteen to make it.

sections.name: Number Sense
sections.instruction: Compare, order, and sort the numbers.

questions.prompt: Which symbol goes in the box?  67 ☐ 76
questions.hint: 67 is smaller than 76. The 'less than' sign points to the smaller number, like a hungry mouth eating the bigger one.
Even numbers can be shared into two equal groups. They end in 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8.

questions.prompt: Put these numbers in order from SMALLEST to largest: 45, 12, 30. Write them with commas.
questions.hint: Find the smallest number first, then the next, then the biggest.

sections.name: Multiplication
sections.instruction: Multiplication is fast adding of equal groups!

questions.prompt: There are 5 groups of 2 apples. How many apples are there in total?
questions.hint: 5 groups of 2 is 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2. Count them all up!

sections.name: Fractions
sections.instruction: Fractions are equal parts of a whole.

questions.prompt: A pizza is cut into 4 equal pieces and you eat 1 piece. What fraction did you eat?
questions.hint: When something is cut into 4 equal parts, each part is called a quarter.

sections.name: Measurement & Calendar
sections.instruction: Think about time, days, and how we measure length.

questions.prompt: How many days are there in one week?
questions.hint: Count them: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday.

questions.prompt: Which month comes right AFTER June?
questions.hint: Say the months in order: ...May, June, then comes the next one.

questions.prompt: How many centimetres (cm) are the same as 1 metre (m)?
questions.hint: One metre is a big step. It is made up of 100 little centimetres.

sections.name: Gathering Data
sections.instruction: Read the tally chart to answer the question.

questions.prompt: A tally chart shows the favourite fruits in a class. Apples have these tallies: llll llll ll (that is one group of 5, another group of 5, and 2 more). How many children chose apples?
questions.hint: Each full group of tally marks is 5. So count 5 + 5 + 2.

questions.prompt: In a race, Ava finished 3rd. What is her position called?
questions.hint: The order is 1st (first), 2nd (second), 3rd (third). She came in 3rd!
